conventions: Each building has its own local origin at its SW outside corner, X east, Y north, Z up from grade. Placement is already solved in your layout; 'conjectural' flags mark designs reconstructed from period Dakota ranch practice.
general_practice_notes: Badlands ranch outbuildings of 1884-86 were round or hewn cottonwood/juniper logs, saddle-notched with long projecting ends, walls 6-7 ft high, roofs of log stringers/poles covered with brush or hay and 6-12 in of clay/sod/scoria, nearly flat (5-12 deg). This matches the barn, blacksmith shop and dugout in T.R.'s photographs.

barn_stables.evidence: Sewall Dec 20 1885: 'We hew the logs on three sides and are putting up two stables 16 x 20 feet with a twelve foot space between like a woods hovel and hay shed.' TAY59 pp.51-56, fig.24; P_STABLE (THRB03296-00401) close-up from S; P_CORRALS from SW. Burned; 18 vertical posts excavated across the N side of the central bay.

length_E_W.source: 20 + 12 + 20 ft; MAP57 burn area 51 ft E-W

depth_N_S.source: Sewall 16; TAY59: roof held up by 'big logs which spanned the space from north to south walls' -> 16 ft span N-S

overall.note: Orientation choice: stables are 20 ft E-W x 16 ft N-S (MAP57 burn extents + N-S roof logs). If your layout already uses 16 E-W x 20 N-S, the overall becomes 44 x 20 ft - P_STABLE's apparent proportions allow either; 52 x 16 is preferred.

central_bay.front: open on the south (buggy/wagon stored inside in P_STABLE)
central_bay.back: closed by closely spaced vertical posts, 18 excavated, 4.75-11 in dia, plus a horizontal log laid against them outside

walls.logs: cottonwood logs hewn on 3 sides (Sewall) - P_STABLE shows rounded outer faces with flattened beds; ~10-12 in

height_to_eave.source: P_STABLE: bay opening ~7 ft at 21.5 px/ft; 7-8 courses

walls.corners: saddle-notched, ends projecting 12-18 in (P_STABLE at bay edges)

doors.position: east end of S wall, edge ~1 ft from SE corner
west part of S wall (hidden behind fence post in P_STABLE; TAY59 'two doors, one in each stable, opened towards the south')

barn_stables.other_openings: small window-like (manure) hatch ~2 x 1.5 ft in the east wall of the east stable (TAY59; probably same in W wall of W stable); feed openings through the inner (bay-side) walls (TAY59 conjecture)
barn_stables.interior: posts dividing stalls and mangers (8 round posts 3.75-7 in excavated in a stable); manure floor

roof.form: very low gable, ridge running N-S over the centre of the bay (front edge in P_STABLE rises ~3-3.5 ft from the ends to the middle)

pitch_deg.derivation: P_STABLE: front edge rises ~75-80 px over ~700-800 px half-width at ~21.5 px/ft -> ~3.5 ft over 26 ft

roof.structure: big N-S log stringers (log ends visible along the S eave at ~8-11 ft spacing) carrying poles laid E-W, then hay/brush and a thin mantle of clay/sod (TAY59; MAT60 'low sloping roof of logs covered with dirt')

south_overhang.source: P_STABLE: roof projects well beyond the stable fronts

roof.on_roof: hay stack ~12 x 10 ft x 5 ft high on the roof over the bay/east stable, reached by a pole ladder (13 rungs, ~11 ft) leaning on the east stable front (P_STABLE)

barn_stables.attached_fences: corral fences abut the barn front at both ends; west stable door opens into one pen, east into another (TAY59)

utility_shed_storehouse.evidence: TAY59 pp.66-67: outline from burned rubble - N 16 ft, S 17'6" ('seems unlikely'), E 24'10", W 25'2"; 'rectangular log building having a low-gabled overhanging roof ... covered with sod or clay. A door opened on the south side, and there may have been windows in the southeast corner'; coal dust and wood chips -> coal/wood store; Henry Walz lived in it in 1898 ('storehouse'); huge pile of cottonwood branches in front (P_CORRALS).

walls.logs: round/hewn cottonwood, saddle-notched (conjectural, by analogy with barn)

roof.form: low gable, ridge N-S, gable facing south over the door (P_CORRALS)

side_overhang.source: TAY59: roof extended far enough to cover the coop entry on the W side

utility_shed_storehouse.context: woodpile of cottonwood branches ~20 ft long x 8 ft high in front (south); coal (lignite) stored inside

chicken_coop_pen.evidence: TAY59 pp.64-67: rectangle of closely set vertical cedar posts, outside N 13'2", S 13'9", W 18'8.5", E 20'0"; E side open (posts only 3'4" from the north) because it abuts the W wall of the shed; posts 3.5-7 in (mostly 4-5 in), set so close a hen could not pass; nest box remains 4 x 3 ft; T.R.: bobcats repeatedly raided the hen house.
chicken_coop_pen.walls: stockade of round cedar posts set in the ground, touching or <2 in gaps, height 5'0"-6'0" (conjectural)
chicken_coop_pen.entry: door between the shed's W wall and the coop's E posts at the north (TAY59 fig.29)
chicken_coop_pen.fittings: nest boxes against the shed wall (box remains 4 x 3 ft)

blacksmith_shop.evidence: TAY59 pp.24-32, fig.7: outside 33'0" (W), 32'8" (E) x 16'0" (N), 16'9" (S) [1959]; Beaubien 1957: 33'9" x 15'?; Mattison card: 33'6" x 15'6"; two rooms: south ~10 x 14'6" inside, north work room 20'6" x 14'6" inside; P_RIVER shows the E side (log ends of the partition), a rectangular brick chimney over the forge, flat sod roof.

Y_from_south_outside.source: inside S room 10 ft + 2 wall logs ~0.75 ft; P_RIVER partition log ends at ~12.7 ft (+/-1.5)

partition.type: log partition, ends visible in E wall

walls.logs: round cottonwood logs ~9-11 in, saddle-notched with short projecting ends (P_RIVER)
walls.south_room_east_wall: logs only about half height, upper half open (TAY59 reading of P_RIVER) -> stall for 1-2 milk cows

roof.structure: pole rafters ~2 ft o.c. (ends visible as a row of light dots under the E eave in P_RIVER) + clay (collapsed roof clay 2-8 in thick found inside)

chimney.type: rectangular brick chimney over the forge (P_RIVER, TAY59)
chimney.position: north room, Y ~25 ft from S end, near the E-W centre/forge stones

openings.type: ordinary door ~2'8" x 6'0" near SE corner into the S room
wide door ~3'6" near NE corner (animals in/out)
narrow door 22 in into N room beside the partition
1-2 windows (glass + frame fragments found near W wall) ~2 x 2 ft

blacksmith_shop.interior: forge on pinkish-red sandstone slabs in N room with brick hearth/chimney (bricks 8 x 3.75 x 2.25 in); work bench along W wall from NW corner ~12 ft, 3 ft deep on 2 posts; ash/slag bin 24-25 in wide against N wall; cottonwood bark spread outside E, W, N walls as footing

dugout_first_shack.evidence: TAY59 pp.20-22, fig.3 (from Beaubien 1957): inside 12 ft N-S x 14 ft E-W; walls of juniper/cottonwood posts 8-12 in set upright side by side; cut into the bank face so earth surrounds 3 sides; exposed E wall with doorway 2'6" wide 'set almost in the middle' (Mattison card: 'only 1 inch off-center'); low gable roof on 3 beams (N wall, S wall, centre beam on posts); roof extended beyond the living space as an overhang over the doorway; sod or scoria roof; horizontal retaining logs against the bank; walls charred above floor. P_RIVER shows the E face with 3 front posts.

walls.type: palisade of upright posts 8-12 in dia, flush; earth-backed on N, S, W

door.position: E wall centred: edges 4'9" and 7'3" from the inside NE corner

roof.form: low gable, ridge E-W on the centre beam (gable faces east toward the river)
roof.beams: 3 log beams E-W (on N wall, S wall, centre on posts)

front_overhang_east.source: P_RIVER: roof carried forward on 3 posts (2 corners + 1 centre in front of the door)

dugout_first_shack.retaining: horizontal logs stacked against the bank on either side of the front (P_RIVER)

round_horse_corral.evidence: T.R. 1888: 'high, circular horse-corral, with a snubbing-post in the center, and a wing built out from one side of the gate entrance, so that the saddle-band can be driven in without trouble'; TAY59 pp.23-24 (Beaubien 1957 excavation).

diameter_outside.source: Beaubien: outside post to outside post

round_horse_corral.posts: cedar posts 5-7 in dia set in PAIRS ~8 in apart (two concentric circles); pairs 10-12 ft apart; 15 sets around the circle; 2 sets of 4 posts mark the gate
round_horse_corral.rails: horizontal poles fastened between each pair (sandwiched), 3-5 in dia; recommend 6 rails, top rail Z 7'0" ('high' corral; conjectural count)
round_horse_corral.gate: swinging gate (gate-hook fragment) at the 4-post set where the wing joins; opening ~10 ft

wing.construction: horizontal poles between the corral and three further pairs of posts

house_enclosure.evidence: TAY59 p.58-62, table 2: single round posts (3.4-6 in, mostly ~4.5 in) at almost exactly 10 ft intervals, 'four spaced horizontal bars nailed to them'; encloses house, well, shed and privy, ~110 x 100 ft; trees used as posts in front of the house; posts 25-33 curve NW along the scoria path
house_enclosure.rails: 4 sawn boards or split poles nailed on the outside face; rails at Z 1'0", 2'0", 3'0", 4'0" (conjectural spacing)

corral_fence_around_barn.evidence: TAY59 p.57: pairs of cedar posts at 10 ft intervals, five horizontal poles fit into the slot between each pair and nailed; area ~100 ft square; gates of sliding poles marked by sets of three posts

x_frame_fence_west.evidence: TAY59 p.63, fig.26 (T.R. photo MWAC_1255_5_10a): 'X' frames set on top of the ground, a horizontal bar spanning between the tops of the Xs, and two other poles nailed to the frame below
x_frame_fence_west.members: X legs ~5.5 ft poles crossing at ~3.75 ft; top rail cradled in the X crotch; 2 lower rails nailed to the legs

well.evidence: TAY59 p.33: 33 ft from the SW corner of the house; oval shaft 4'6" diameter, stone-lined; top 'surrounded with a small rectangular enclosure, for the base logs were still intact'; choked within 6 ft of the top in 1959; depth unknown.

depth.source: conjectural: terrace is 13-15 ft above the streambed (TAY59 p.6); water near river level

curb_enclosure.plan: rectangular log curb of base logs ~6'0" x 5'6" outside (conjectural size)
curb_enclosure.cover: plank lid; windlass or bucket-and-rope (no evidence; omit or keep minimal)

privy.evidence: not found by excavation (TAY59 p.17); north of the house inside the fence along the scoria path
privy.recommendation: conjectural 4'0" x 4'6" board privy, shed roof, ~7 ft high; or omit
